_meta: 2025 state individual income tax, single filer, simplified for calculator estimates. Sources: Tax Foundation 2025 State Income Tax Rates and Brackets; state revenue dept publications. Brackets = [[upper_bound, marginal_rate], ...]; last entry upper_bound 0 = no cap. std_ded = state standard deduction (single); use federal-style 0 where state relies on exemptions.
source: Tax Foundation 2025 State Income Tax Rates and Brackets (taxfoundation.org), state revenue departments

al.name: Alabama
al.note: Alabama keeps a low $3,000 standard deduction, so state tax starts on almost all wage income.

ak.name: Alaska
ak.note: Alaska levies no state income tax and pays residents a Permanent Fund Dividend most years.

az.name: Arizona
az.note: Arizona's 2.5% flat tax took full effect in 2023 and pairs with a federal-size standard deduction.

ar.name: Arkansas
ar.note: Arkansas exempts its first bracket and taxes the rest at up to 3.9%.

ca.name: California
ca.note: California runs the nation's most brackets, from 1% to 12.3%, plus a 1% mental-health surcharge above $1M.

co.name: Colorado
co.note: Colorado taxes taxable income at a flat 4.4% after federal-style deductions.

ct.name: Connecticut
ct.note: Connecticut phases out its standard deduction at higher incomes, raising effective rates.

de.name: Delaware
de.note: Delaware has no sales tax but a graduated income tax reaching 6.6%.

fl.name: Florida
fl.note: Florida has no personal income tax; it funds government via sales tax and tourism.

ga.name: Georgia
ga.note: Georgia moved to a 5.19% flat rate for 2025, down from 5.39%.

hi.name: Hawaii
hi.note: Hawaii restructured brackets in 2025 and still tops out at 11%.

id.name: Idaho
id.note: Idaho's flat rate has been cut repeatedly, landing at 5.3% for 2025.

il.name: Illinois
il.note: Illinois' 4.95% flat rate is locked into the state constitution.

in.name: Indiana
in.note: Indiana's rate falls to 3.00% in 2025 and is scheduled to keep dropping.

ia.name: Iowa
ia.note: Iowa consolidated to a 3.8% flat rate in 2025 after years of graduated brackets.

ks.name: Kansas
ks.note: Kansas collapsed its brackets to a single 5.7% rate.

ky.name: Kentucky
ky.note: Kentucky's flat tax fell to 4.0% in 2025 and is set to drop further.

la.name: Louisiana
la.note: Louisiana's 2025 reform created a 3% flat tax with a $12,500 standard deduction.

me.name: Maine
me.note: Maine uses three brackets and a federal-style standard deduction.

md.name: Maryland
md.note: Maryland counties add roughly 2.25%–3.2% local income tax on top of state rates.

ma.name: Massachusetts
ma.note: Massachusetts taxes salary at 5%, with a 4% surtax only above $1M.

mi.name: Michigan
mi.note: Michigan cut its flat rate to 4.25% for 2025.

mn.name: Minnesota
mn.note: Minnesota's top rate of 9.85% is among the highest in the Midwest.

ms.name: Mississippi
ms.note: Mississippi taxes income at a flat 4.4% for 2025, scheduled to fall to 4.25%.

mo.name: Missouri
mo.note: Missouri exempts its first roughly $1,300 of taxable income and tops out near 4.7%.

mt.name: Montana
mt.note: Montana rebated 2024 taxes and lowered its top rate to 5.9% for 2025 onward.

ne.name: Nebraska
ne.note: Nebraska's top rate fell to 5.2% in 2025 with further cuts triggered.

nv.name: Nevada
nv.note: Nevada has no income tax; it relies on gaming and sales taxes.

nh.name: New Hampshire
nh.note: New Hampshire fully repealed its interest-and-dividends tax as of January 1, 2025 — wages were never taxed.

nj.name: New Jersey
nj.note: New Jersey pairs seven brackets with generous personal exemptions instead of a standard deduction.

nm.name: New Mexico
nm.note: New Mexico's 2025 reform raised its standard deduction to $15,480 for single filers.

ny.name: New York
ny.note: New York City residents add a local income tax of roughly 3%–3.9% on top of state rates.

nc.name: North Carolina
nc.note: North Carolina's flat rate and $12,750 standard deduction keep state tax modest.

nd.name: North Dakota
nd.note: North Dakota taxes its first bracket at 0% and tops out at just 2.5%.

oh.name: Ohio
oh.note: Ohio's 2025 cuts zero out the first bracket below $26,050 of income.

ok.name: Oklahoma
ok.note: Oklahoma keeps six narrow low-rate brackets before reaching 4.75%.

or.name: Oregon
or.note: Oregon has no sales tax but one of the highest top income-tax rates at 9.9%.

pa.name: Pennsylvania
pa.note: Pennsylvania's 3.07% flat rate is the lowest flat rate among states that tax wages.

ri.name: Rhode Island
ri.note: Rhode Island's top rate of 5.99% starts above roughly $172,000.

sc.name: South Carolina
sc.note: South Carolina exempts its first $3,560 (2025 zero bracket) then taxes at up to 6.2%.

sd.name: South Dakota
sd.note: South Dakota has levied no individual income tax since 1976 (a 2024 repeal vote failed).

tn.name: Tennessee
tn.note: Tennessee completed its repeal of the Hall income tax — wages and investments are untaxed.

tx.name: Texas
tx.note: Texas levies no income tax; property taxes are among the highest in the country instead.

ut.name: Utah
ut.note: Utah taxes income at 4.55% and phases out its personal exemption at higher incomes (a tax-credit system).

vt.name: Vermont
vt.note: Vermont's top rate of 8.75% applies above $242,000.

va.name: Virginia
va.note: Virginia's standard deduction jumped to $8,750 for 2025 under recent legislation.

wa.name: Washington
wa.note: Washington taxes wages at 0%; only large capital gains face a 7% excise tax.

wv.name: West Virginia
wv.note: West Virginia has been cutting rates toward a goal of eventually eliminating its income tax.

wi.name: Wisconsin
wi.note: Wisconsin's private-school and childcare credits can cut effective tax well below bracket rates.

wy.name: Wyoming
wy.note: Wyoming funds the state largely through mineral severance taxes — no income tax.
